name: Reply Tug
summary: A group chat where you tug a bubble right to quote it in your reply, or pull left to see the times
about: A phone group chat for cousins planning Eid lunch, built around the swipe-to-reply gesture. Drag any message to the right and a reply arrow grows behind it, its ring filling until it pops; let go and the bubble springs back while a quote card slides up above the text box. Send your answer and it rises out of the composer with its ticks turning blue, then a cousin types back and quotes you.
how: Drag a message to the right until the arrow ring fills, then let go to quote it; on a keyboard, focus a message and press R or Enter.
Type your reply and press Enter or the send button: watch the clock become one tick, two ticks and then blue ticks before a cousin answers.
Pull the whole chat to the left to peek at the time of every message, or press T or the clock button to keep the times shown.
Tap a quote inside a bubble to jump to the original message, which flashes; Escape or the cross cancels a reply.
